tools.name: get_listing
tools.description: Get the full record of one listing found with search_listings. Returns everything in the search result plus the seller's description, color, material, minimum offer, the on-chain provenance record (fingerprint and what it does and does not prove), when it was listed, and how to buy it: the checkout

tools.description: Quote what a listing costs in a crypto asset right now. Asks NEAR Intents solvers how much of `pay_with` the buyer would send so the seller receives the listing's exact USD price (postage included) in USDC. Returns the piece, its USD price, the amount and asset to pay with its USD value, what the se

tools.name: start_purchase
tools.description: Reserve a listing for the signed-in buyer and get a one-time NEAR Intents deposit address and the exact amount of `pay_with` to send. Nothing is charged by this call: the purchase completes only when the buyer's own wallet sends that exact amount to that address before the deadline. Returns a checko

tools.name: purchase_status
tools.description: Check a purchase started with start_purchase. Returns its state: awaiting_deposit (send the amount), deposit_seen, processing, paid (the order is recorded and the seller was paid), refunded (funds returned to refund_to), failed, expired (deadline passed without a deposit) or review (being checked by

tools.name: report_deposit
tools.description: Optionally tell Port66 the transaction hash of the buyer's deposit for a purchase, so NEAR Intents spots the payment sooner. Not required: deposits are detected on their own. Does not move money or change the amount due. Returns the purchase's current state. Safe to call more than once. Requires a P

tools.name: make_offer
tools.description: Send the seller an offer below the listed price, with an optional note. The seller has 24 hours to accept, decline or counter; check with offer_status. If accepted, start_purchase uses the agreed price. Returns the offer id, its status and when it expires. Respect the listing's minimum_offer from ge

tools.name: offer_status
tools.description: Check the signed-in buyer's latest offer on a listing made with make_offer. Returns the offer's amount in USD, its status (for example pending, accepted, declined or expired) and expiry, plus agreed_price_usd: the price start_purchase will charge if the seller accepted, otherwise null. Returns offer

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "start_purchase" references sensitive artifacts (authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Reserve a listing for the signed-in buyer and get a one-time NEAR Intents deposit address and the exact amount of `pay_with` to send. Nothing is charged by this…

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_listings, get_listing, purchase_status · Private data: get_listing, start_purchase · Public sink: price_in_crypto, start_purchase, purchase_status, make_offer.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_listings, get_listing, purchase_status · Private data: get_listing, start_purchase · Public sink: price_in_crypto, start_purchase, purchase_status, make_offer

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_listings" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
